answers.how: Measured the yellow car’s displacement around 2.5 s and converted using the white car’s acceleration-based scale, correcting for depth and direction.
Measured the road cross-section, corrected its perspective, and divided the two-lane width by two.
Measured the white car’s longitudinal extent and calibrated it from its pixel acceleration of 4 m/s².
Compared the yellow car’s longitudinal pixel extent with the calibrated white car, correcting for their different depths.
Measured the yellow car’s vertical extent relative to its wheel-contact plane and applied the depth-corrected scale.
Measured approximately 12 pixels across a bicycle wheel and applied the calibrated scale at the bicycle’s depth.
Measured the traffic light from its ground base to its top and corrected for ground-plane perspective.
Measured streetlight base-to-top extents and converted using their perspective-adjusted ground positions.
Tracked the pedestrian from the first to the last frame, corrected the displacement for depth, and divided by 2.958 seconds.
Measured approximately 50 pixels from head to feet and applied the calibrated scale at the pedestrian’s depth.
Tracked the bicycle across the clip and converted its displacement using the acceleration-calibrated, depth-corrected scale.
